title: Hematovascular and Anti-Leukemic Profiling of Dolomiaea costus Root Extracts in Zebrafish Embryos: Dissociation of Erythroid and Vascular Phenotypes with GATA1-Guided Prioritization of Dehydrocostus Lactone
content: Dolomiaea costus (Indian costus) is rich in sesquiterpene lactones with reported anticancer and anti-angiogenic activity, yet whether crude root extracts reproduce these effects in an intact developing vertebrate and whether such effects extend to leukemia cells and a plausible molecular target not been examined in an integrated model. Here, zebrafish embryos exposed to n-hexane, chloroform, ethyl acetate or methanol D. costus root extracts showed a marked, extract-dependent reduction in hemoglobin-associated (o-dianisidine) staining at 72 h post-fertilization (hpf) (Kruskal–Wallis P = 0.0017), most pronounced for n-hexane and chloroform (6.4% and 8.2% of control, respectively). Unexpectedly, this profound hematopoietic phenotype was not accompanied by a reduction in intersegmental or sub-intestinal vessel number in Tg(fli1:EGFP) reporter larvae, despite pronounced pericardial edema, indicating that the erythroid/hematopoietic and vascular-patterning responses to this extract are dissociable. Early-onset n-hexane exposure produced a substantially larger staining deficit than exposure beginning at 48 hpf (P = 0.0081), consistent with a developmentally sensitive window. In parallel, all four extracts reduced MTT-measured viability in Jurkat and THP-1 leukemia cells, with n-hexane the most potent (sub-micromolar fitted IC₅₀). Molecular docking against two independent GATA1 zinc-finger structures ranked dehydrocostus lactonethe dominant GC–MS constituent of the active extracts above three reference GATA-directed inhibitors in a zebrafish Gata1 model, nominating it as a candidate driver of the observed phenotype. Together, these findings provide integrated phenotypic and computational evidence linking D. costus root extracts to a selective hematopoietic/erythroid vulnerability, anti-leukemic cytotoxicity, and a GATA1-centered mechanistic hypothesis, establishing a prioritized lead compound and a hematovascular screening framework for future natural-product-based anti-leukemic drug discovery.
